rows.stem: Water in the root enters due to :

options.label: A
options.text: the function of the root to absorb water.

options.label: B
options.text: difference in the concentration of ions between the root and the soil.

options.label: C
options.text: excess water present in the soil.

options.label: D
options.text: diffusion of water in the roots.

rows.solution:
The root cells in contact with the soil actively take up ions. This creates a difference in the concentration of these ions between the root and the soil. Water therefore moves into the root from the soil to remove this difference.

This is option (B) difference in the concentration of ions between the root and the soil.

rows.stem: Which one of the given statements is incorrect :

options.label: A
options.text: DNA has the complete information for a particular characteristic.

options.label: B
options.text: DNA is the molecule responsible for the inheritance of characters from parents to offsprings.

options.label: C
options.text: Change in information will produce a different protein.

options.label: D
options.text: Characteristics will remain the same even if protein changes.

rows.solution:
DNA carries the information for making proteins, and the proteins control the characteristics. If the information changes, a different protein is made, and the characteristic changes too: for example, a less efficient enzyme for a plant hormone gives a shorter plant. So it is incorrect to say that characteristics stay the same when the protein changes.

The incorrect statement is option (D) Characteristics will remain the same even if protein changes.

rows.stem: Sensory nerve of a reflex arc carries information from the receptor cells to the :
rows.solution:
In a reflex arc, the sensory nerve carries the message from the receptor to the spinal cord, where the relay neurons pass it to the motor nerve, which carries it to the effector muscles.

This is option (A) spinal cord.

rows.stem: An alpha particle enters a uniform magnetic field as shown. The direction of motion of the alpha particle is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the directions are given only in the drawing: four parallel arrowed lines labelled Magnetic Field and one arrowed line labelled alpha-particle crossing them at right angles; the sense of the field and of the particle's path is withheld here because it decides the answer. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
In the figure the magnetic field lines point to the left and the alpha particle enters moving up the page. The particle's motion at entry is up the page, which no option offers, so the question means the direction of the force on the particle, which is what all four options describe.

An alpha particle is positively charged, so the direction of its motion is the direction of the current. By Fleming's left-hand rule (forefinger along the field, to the left; middle finger along the current, up the page), the thumb points out of the page. So the force on the alpha particle, and the direction in which it starts to bend, is out of the page.

This is option (D) out of the page.

rows.stem: Name a plant hormone responsible for bending of a shoot of a plant when it is exposed to unidirectional light. How does it promote phototropism ?
rows.solution:
The hormone is auxin. It is synthesised at the tip of the shoot.

When light falls on the shoot from one side, auxin diffuses towards the shady side of the shoot. The higher concentration of auxin there stimulates the cells on the shady side to grow longer than those on the side facing the light. So the shoot bends towards the light (positive phototropism).

rows.stem: What is the other name of ‘tissue fluid’ ? Write its two functions.
rows.solution:
Tissue fluid is also called lymph.

Two functions:

1. Lymph carries digested and absorbed fat from the intestine (through the lymph capillaries in the villi).

2. It drains the excess fluid from the spaces between the cells (the extracellular space) back into the blood.

rows.stem: “Although gardens are created by man but they are considered to be an ecosystem.” Justify this statement.
rows.solution:
An ecosystem is made of all the living organisms in an area together with the non-living components of their environment, interacting with each other.

A garden has biotic components such as plants (grasses, trees, flowering plants), animals (insects, birds, earthworms) and decomposers (bacteria, fungi). These living organisms interact with each other and with the abiotic components such as water, air, soil, sunlight and temperature: the plants make food, the animals feed on them, and the decomposers return the nutrients to the soil. So a garden works as an ecosystem, even though it is made by man (an artificial ecosystem).

rows.stem:
Consider the following salts :

(i) \(\mathrm{YCl}\) (ii) \(\mathrm{NH_4X}\) (iii) \(\mathrm{ZCO_3}\)

(a) What would be the pH of the salt solution if in \(\mathrm{YCl}\), Y is sodium ? Give reason for your answer.

(b) If in salt \(\mathrm{NH_4X}\), X is nitrate, then its solution will give what colour with universal indicator ? Why ?

(c) What would be the change in colour in blue litmus solution if \(\mathrm{ZCO_3}\) is added to it and Z is potassium ?
rows.solution:
(a) With Y as sodium the salt is sodium chloride, NaCl. It is the salt of a strong acid (HCl) and a strong base (NaOH), so its solution is neutral, with pH = 7.

(b) With X as nitrate the salt is ammonium nitrate, \(\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}\). It is the salt of a strong acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)) and a weak base (\(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\)), so its solution is acidic, with pH less than 7, and it turns universal indicator orange (or pink).

(c) The formula \(\mathrm{ZCO_3}\) does not fit potassium: potassium has a valency of 1, so potassium carbonate is \(\mathrm{K_2CO_3}\). The answer below is for \(\mathrm{K_2CO_3}\).

Potassium carbonate is the salt of a strong base (KOH) and a weak acid (\(\mathrm{H_2CO_3}\)), so its solution is basic, with pH more than 7. A basic solution does not change the colour of blue litmus, so the litmus solution remains blue: there is no change.

rows.stem: The magnification produced when an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from a spherical mirror is \(+1/2\). Where should the object be placed to reduce the magnification to \(+1/3\).
rows.solution:
A positive magnification means the image is virtual and erect. For \(u = -20\) cm and \(m = +\dfrac{1}{2}\),

\(m = -\dfrac{v}{u}\), so \(v = -m \times u = -\dfrac{1}{2} \times (-20) = +10\) cm.

By the mirror formula,

\(\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{20}\), so \(f = +20\) cm.

The focal length is positive, so the mirror is convex (it gives a diminished, erect, virtual image).

For \(m = +\dfrac{1}{3}\), let the new object and image distances be \(u'\) and \(v'\). Then \(\dfrac{1}{3} = -\dfrac{v'}{u'}\), so \(v' = -\dfrac{u'}{3}\).

\(\dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{v'} + \dfrac{1}{u'} = -\dfrac{3}{u'} + \dfrac{1}{u'} = -\dfrac{2}{u'}\), so \(u' = -40\) cm.

The object should be placed 40 cm in front of the mirror. (Check: \(v' = \dfrac{40}{3}\) cm, and \(\dfrac{3}{40} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{20}\).)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Define the term dispersion of white light. State the colour which bends (i) the most, (ii) the least while passing through a glass prism. Draw a diagram to show the dispersion of white light.
rows.solution:
Dispersion of white light is the splitting of white light into its seven constituent colours as it passes through a glass prism.

(i) Violet bends the most.

(ii) Red bends the least.

Diagram: draw a triangular glass prism. A ray of white light falls on one face and, on entering the glass, splits into a band of colours. The rays leave from the other face, bending towards the base, and fall on a screen as a spectrum: red at the top (least deviated), then orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet at the bottom (most deviated). Label the white light, the prism and the colours (VIBGYOR), and put arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
Write the chemical equation for the following :

(i) Combustion of methane

(ii) Oxidation of ethanol

(iii) Hydrogenation of ethene

(iv) Esterification Reaction

(v) Saponification Reaction
rows.solution:
(i) Combustion of methane:

\(\mathrm{CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O}\) + heat and light

(ii) Oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid, by alkaline potassium permanganate or acidified potassium dichromate on heating:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4 \text{ or acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

(iii) Hydrogenation of ethene, in the presence of a nickel (or palladium or platinum) catalyst, gives ethane:

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2 \xrightarrow{Ni} CH_3{-}CH_3}\)

(iv) Esterification: ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to give the sweet-smelling ester ethyl ethanoate and water:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } H_2SO_4} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

(The marking scheme's equation leaves out the water; without it the equation does not balance.)

(v) Saponification: the ester reacts with sodium hydroxide to give back the alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + C_2H_5OH}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Draw two structural isomers of butane.

(ii) Draw the structures of propanol and propanone.

(iii) Name the third homologue of :

(a) alcohols

(b) aldehydes

(iv) Name the following :

(a) the structure drawn in the attached figure

(b) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2CH=CH_2}\)

(v) Show the covalent bond formation in nitrogen molecule.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (iv)(a) asks to name a compound given only as a drawn structural formula: six C atoms in a ring, each carrying one H, joined by alternating single and double bonds. It is not typed here, per the rule that structures are figures, and its name is the answer. Part (iv)(b) is typed. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
(i) Butane, \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\), has two structural isomers:

n-butane, a straight chain of four carbon atoms, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\): the end carbons carry three hydrogen atoms each and the middle carbons two each.

isobutane (2-methylpropane), a chain of three carbon atoms with the fourth carbon attached to the middle one, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_3}\): the middle carbon carries one hydrogen and each of the other three carbons carries three.

(ii) Propanol, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}OH}\): a chain of three carbon atoms, the first carrying three hydrogen atoms and the other two carrying two each, with an \(\mathrm{-OH}\) group on the end carbon. (The marking scheme's condensed alternative, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2OH}\), is ethanol; propanol has three carbon atoms.)

Propanone, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CO{-}CH_3}\): a chain of three carbon atoms in which the middle carbon carries a double-bonded oxygen and each end carbon carries three hydrogen atoms.

(iii) (a) The alcohols run methanol, ethanol, propanol, so the third homologue is propanol, \(\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}\).

(b) The aldehydes run methanal, ethanal, propanal, so the third homologue is propanal, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5CHO}\).

(iv) (a) A ring of six carbon atoms, each carrying one hydrogen, with alternating single and double bonds, is benzene, \(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\).

(b) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH{=}CH_2}\) has four carbon atoms and a double bond, so it is butene (but-1-ene).

(v) A nitrogen atom (2, 5) has five valence electrons and needs three more to complete its octet. Two nitrogen atoms share three pairs of electrons, forming a triple bond, \(\mathrm{N{\equiv}N}\). In the electron dot structure, three dots and three crosses (three shared pairs) lie in the overlap between the two atoms, and each nitrogen keeps one lone pair of its own, so each has eight electrons around it.
